territorial_scope.description: Applies within Chile; Article 7 requires registration with a Chilean public health institute before neurotechnologies are used on people.

evidence.quote: Las neurotecnologías deberán ser previamente registradas por el Instituto de Salud Pública para su uso en las personas.

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health
agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Senate-approved Chilean bill (Boletín 13.828-19) on neurorights. Would require prior registration of neurotechnologies with the Instituto de Salud Pública, consent for interventions on others, and treat neural data as sensitive data; allows health authority to restrict uses; sets producer liability and criminal offences. Takes effect six months after publication.
summary.long: The bill (Boletín N° 13.828-19, Senate-approved text communicated 7 December 2021) sets rules for neurotechnologies and neural data, with stated purpose the protection of life and physical and psychic integrity (Art. 1). Under Art. 7, neurotechnologies must be registered in advance with the Instituto de Salud Pública before use on people. Art. 4 requires free, prior and informed consent, expressed in writing and essentially revocable, to use neurotechnology on another person. Art. 6 requires installation and operation to be essentially reversible, except therapeutic uses. Art. 8 allows the health authority, by reasoned resolution, to restrict or prohibit uses in listed cases, including influencing behaviour without consent, exploiting vulnerabilities, unauthorised data extraction and harm to the neuroplasticity of children and adolescents. Art. 9 makes producers, providers and administrators jointly and objectively liable for damage, with listed exemptions. Art. 10 sets criminal offences with presidio penalties. Art. 11 treats neural data as generally confidential and as sensitive data under Law 19.628. Arts. 13 to 15 amend Laws 20.120 and 19.628 and the electoral law. Art. 12 provides for a Ministry of Health regulation. The law enters into force six months after publication in the Diario Oficial.

notes: Document is the Senate's transmittal (Valparaíso, 7 Dec 2021) of the Senate-approved bill to the Chamber of Deputies, not a consolidated text. Target instrument IDs are not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is empty. Ley 20.120 and Ley 19.628 each appear once, as amends; their other textual references are noted in the notes field. Art. 15 was approved by 26 of 40 senators, which the transmittal states satisfies Constitution art. 66 para. 2. The unnumbered transitional article sets entry into force six months after publication in the Diario Oficial and requires the Art. 12 regulation within that period.

thresholds.note: The bill has no numeric cutoff that changes the legal treatment of a person. The numbers in the text are a six-month entry-into-force period (transitory article, a procedural deadline and an event), penalty grades in Art. 10 (enforcement), and legislative vote counts in the Senate communication (procedural, not coded). Art. 8 restrictions and Art. 9 liability are not numeric, and the Art. 12 regulation is not delegated with a numeric threshold.
